practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice of India?
opts: Article 124
Article 126
Article 127
Article 128
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 126 of the Constitution of India deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice. When the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant or when the Chief Justice is, by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of their office, the President shall appoint such one of the other judges of the Court as the President deems fit to perform the duties of the office. Article 124 deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court, Article 127 deals with ad hoc judges, and Article 128 deals with retired judges sitting in the Supreme Court.

practiceQuestions.q: Who is constitutionally empowered to appoint the Acting Chief Justice of India?
opts: The Prime Minister of India
The President of India
The Collegium of the Supreme Court
The Union Minister of Law and Justice
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 126, the President of India holds the constitutional power to appoint an Acting Chief Justice of India when the office of CJI is vacant or the incumbent is unable to discharge their duties.

practiceQuestions.q: Under what primary circumstances is an Acting Chief Justice appointed under Article 126?
opts: When a motion for impeachment against the CJI is initiated
When the office of CJI is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform duties due to absence or other reasons
When the Supreme Court faces a heavy backlog of pending cases
When all sitting judges of the Supreme Court recommend a temporary replacement
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 126 explicitly states that an Acting CJI is appointed when the office of the Chief Justice is vacant, or when the Chief Justice is, by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of their office.

practiceQuestions.q: Can a person who is not a judge of the Supreme Court be appointed as the Acting Chief Justice of India?
opts: Yes, any senior advocate can be appointed.
Yes, any High Court Chief Justice can be appointed directly.
No, only one of the other judges of the Supreme Court can be appointed.
Yes, with the prior concurrence of the Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 126 mandates that the President shall appoint 'such one of the other judges of the Court' to perform the duties of the Chief Justice. Therefore, an Acting CJI must be a sitting judge of the Supreme Court.

practiceQuestions.q: What oath or affirmation is taken by an Acting Chief Justice of India upon appointment?
opts: A fresh oath administered by the Prime Minister
No separate oath is required if they have already taken an oath as a Supreme Court judge under the Third Schedule.
A special oath administered by the Speaker of Lok Sabha
An oath administered by the Union Law Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: Since judges of the Supreme Court already take an oath under the Third Schedule of the Constitution (wherein they swear to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution and perform their duties without fear or favour), a judge appointed as Acting CJI does not take a brand-new oath specifically for the temporary office, as they are already a sworn Supreme Court judge.

practiceQuestions.q: During the tenure of an Acting Chief Justice of India, what happens to their salary and allowances?
opts: They receive the salary and allowances specified for the Chief Justice of India.
They continue to receive only the salary of a puisne Supreme Court judge.
They receive a reduced salary because the position is temporary.
Their salary is determined exclusively by the Parliamentary Committee on Salaries.
practiceQuestions.sol: According to the Second Schedule of the Constitution and relevant parliamentary enactments governing Supreme Court judges' salaries, while acting as the Chief Justice of India, the judge is entitled to the salary, allowances, and privileges applicable to the Chief Justice of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Does the Acting Chief Justice of India possess all the administrative and judicial powers of a regular Chief Justice?
opts: No, they can only hear constitutional bench matters and cannot perform administrative tasks.
Yes, they exercise all administrative and judicial powers vested in the Chief Justice of India.
No, they cannot constitute benches or allocate cases to other judges.
Yes, but only with the prior approval of the Union Law Ministry for administrative decisions.
practiceQuestions.sol: An Acting Chief Justice performs all the duties and exercises all the powers of the Chief Justice of India, including master of the rolls functions such as constituting benches, assigning cases, and heading administrative committees.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional body or functionary advises the President on the appointment of judges, which indirectly influences or precedes the line of succession for Acting CJI?
opts: The Supreme Court Collegium headed by the CJI
The Law Commission of India
The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)
The Attorney General of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court Collegium recommends appointments to the Supreme Court. While Article 126 does not explicitly mention the Collegium for selecting the Acting CJI, convention and seniority dictate that the senior-most available judge of the Supreme Court is appointed, a process tied to the institutional framework overseen by the CJI and the Collegium.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the typical tenure of an Acting Chief Justice of India?
opts: A fixed term of 5 years
Until the age of 65 years
Temporary, lasting until the regular CJI resumes office or a new CJI is appointed
A fixed term of 1 year, renewable once
practiceQuestions.sol: The tenure of an Acting Chief Justice is strictly temporary and ad-interim. It terminates as soon as the regular Chief Justice resumes their duties or a new permanent Chief Justice is appointed to office.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of the Indian Supreme Court, which convention is traditionally followed in selecting the judge to be appointed as Acting Chief Justice?
opts: Appointment of the judge with the highest number of written judgments
Appointment of the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court
Election by a secret ballot among Supreme Court judges
Nomination by the Law Minister in consultation with the Prime Minister
practiceQuestions.sol: Following the convention of seniority that applies to the appointment of the regular Chief Justice of India, the President appoints the senior-most sitting judge of the Supreme Court as the Acting Chief Justice.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the institution of the Acting Chief Justice under Article 126 ensure the principle of continuous institutional functioning of the judiciary?
opts: By preventing administrative paralysis and judicial vacuum when the permanent CJI is incapacitated or the office falls vacant unexpectedly.
By allowing the executive to directly intervene in high-profile judicial cases during leadership crises.
By granting supreme legislative powers to the Supreme Court during emergencies.
By dissolving the collegium system temporarily until a new permanent CJI is chosen.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Supreme Court requires continuous administrative oversight, such as roster allocation, urgent listing of matters, and functioning of administrative committees. Article 126 acts as a constitutional safety valve preventing any interregnum or leadership vacuum that could cripple judicial administration.

practiceQuestions.q: What distinguishes an Acting Chief Justice appointed under Article 126 from an 'Ad-hoc Judge' appointed under Article 127 of the Constitution?
opts: Acting CJI is chosen from sitting Supreme Court judges to lead the court, whereas ad-hoc judges are High Court judges brought in temporarily to constitute a quorum.
Acting CJI has no voting rights in judicial benches, while ad-hoc judges have full administrative powers.
Acting CJI is appointed by the Parliament, whereas ad-hoc judges are appointed by the Prime Minister.
There is no functional difference; both terms are used interchangeably in the Constitution.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 126 deals with an Acting CJI who performs the duties of the head of the institution and is chosen from sitting Supreme Court judges. Article 127 deals with ad-hoc judges where, if there is a lack of a quorum of permanent Supreme Court judges to hold or continue any session of the Court, the CJI (with previous consent of the President and Chief Justice of a High Court) may request a qualified HC judge to attend sittings as an ad-hoc judge.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does Article 126 specifically empower the President to appoint the Acting CJI rather than leaving it strictly to an automatic internal judicial succession?
opts: To maintain the system of checks and balances and formalize executive-judicial coordination in a constitutional democracy.
Because the President holds absolute veto power over judicial appointments under the Basic Structure doctrine.
To ensure that the ruling political party can select a judge favourable to its policies.
Because the Supreme Court lacks any internal mechanism to determine seniority.
practiceQuestions.sol: In India's constitutional framework, even though judicial independence is paramount, the formal head of state (the President) makes executive appointments based on constitutional provisions. This maintains constitutional propriety and links the highest judicial office to the formal warrant of appointment by the Executive, while convention guides that the senior-most judge is chosen.

practiceQuestions.q: In the historical evolution of the Indian Supreme Court, have there been instances where Acting Chief Justices played crucial roles during sudden vacancies?
opts: No, the office of Acting CJI has never been invoked in the history of independent India.
Yes, on several occasions when sitting CJIs passed away in office, resigned, or retired unexpectedly without an immediate successor being sworn in simultaneously.
Only during the Emergency of 1975-1977 was an Acting CJI ever appointed.
Only when the Parliament passes a special resolution requesting a temporary Chief Justice.
Only during the Emergency of 1975-1977 was an Acting CJI ever appointed.
Only when the Parliament passes a special resolution requesting a temporary Chief Justice.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 126 has been invoked multiple times in India's judicial history. For instance, when a CJI dies in office or retires and the formal transition encounters a brief gap, or when a CJI is unwell, an Acting CJI is appointed to ensure uninterrupted judicial work.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the power of an Acting Chief Justice regarding the constitution of benches (Master of Roster) compare to that of a permanent Chief Justice?
opts: An Acting CJI possesses identical authority as the Master of the Roster, meaning all bench formations and case allocations ordered by them are fully valid.
An Acting CJI cannot allocate public interest litigations (PILs), only regular civil and criminal appeals.
An Acting CJI must consult all other Supreme Court judges before constituting any bench.
An Acting CJI is strictly prohibited from forming Constitution Benches.
practiceQuestions.sol: Since Article 126 empowers the Acting CJI to 'perform the duties of the office' of the Chief Justice, they step into the full institutional role, which includes the exclusive administrative prerogative of being the Master of the Roster. Their administrative decisions regarding benches and case allocation carry full legal and judicial validity.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the relationship between the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice under Article 126 and the principle of judicial independence?
opts: Judicial independence is safeguarded by adhering strictly to the seniority convention, preventing executive arbitrariness in selecting the Acting CJI.
Judicial independence is compromised because the President can choose any junior judge regardless of seniority.
Article 126 subordinates the judiciary directly to the Ministry of Law and Justice during a vacancy.
The Acting CJI has no independence and must seek Cabinet approval for judgements.
practiceQuestions.sol: Even though the power is formally vested in the Executive (President), convention dictates that the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is invariably appointed as Acting CJI. This prevents executive cherry-picking and preserves the institutional independence of the judiciary.

practiceQuestions.q: If a permanent vacancy arises in the office of CJI, does the appointment of an Acting CJI under Article 126 serve as a permanent solution or a stop-gap arrangement?
opts: It serves as a permanent replacement once the Acting CJI completes one year in office.
It is strictly a stop-gap arrangement until a regular Chief Justice of India is formally appointed according to established constitutional procedures.
It automatically converts into a permanent Chief Justice position after Cabinet ratification.
It transforms into a permanent post if the Supreme Court Collegium passes a unanimous resolution.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Acting CJI is purely an interim arrangement. The constitutional machinery requires that a regular, permanent Chief Justice be appointed through the standard Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) involving the Collegium and the Executive.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the scope of 'duties of his office' that an Acting CJI is mandated to perform under Article 126?
opts: Only administrative responsibilities, excluding participation in judicial bench hearings.
Only criminal appellate jurisdiction matters.
The entire spectrum of both judicial adjudications and administrative leadership duties associated with the office of CJI.
Advisory jurisdiction cases referred solely by the President under Article 143.
practiceQuestions.sol: An Acting Chief Justice assumes the entire portfolio of the Chief Justice of India, encompassing both judicial duties (hearing cases, heading benches) and administrative duties (managing court administration, recommending appointments, heading committees).

practiceQuestions.q: If a sitting judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as Acting CJI, does it create a permanent vacancy in their original seat as a puisne judge of the Supreme Court?
opts: Yes, a new judge must be appointed to fill their former position permanently.
No, they continue to hold their position as a Supreme Court judge while temporarily performing the duties of the CJI.
Yes, and they must resign from their puisne judge position before taking up the Acting CJI role.
No, but their pension benefits are frozen during the temporary appointment.
practiceQuestions.sol: An Acting CJI is simply performing additional temporary duties attached to the leadership of the court. They do not vacate their substantive post as a Supreme Court judge; once the regular CJI returns or a new one is appointed, the Acting CJI reverts to discharging their normal duties as a judge of the Supreme Court.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the provision of Acting Chief Justice under Article 126 reflect the framers' foresight regarding institutional continuity?
opts: By acknowledging that the highest judicial tribunal cannot afford any disruption in leadership, thereby embedding an internal operational fallback mechanism.
By giving absolute supremacy to the legislature over judicial functioning during a crisis.
By allowing the President to dissolve the Supreme Court if the CJI position is vacant for over a month.
By establishing a provision where retired judges automatically assume control of the Supreme Court.
practiceQuestions.sol: The framers of the Constitution anticipated potential disruptions such as illness, sudden demise, resignation, or transition gaps between Chief Justices. Article 126 was crafted specifically to ensure that the apex court never faces a leadership vacuum, guaranteeing uninterrupted delivery of justice.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Acting Chief Justice of India:
1. The office of the Acting Chief Justice of India is created under Article 126 of the Constitution.
2. An Acting Chief Justice can only be appointed from amongst the retired judges of the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 126 provides for the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice by the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: An Acting Chief Justice must be appointed from 'amongst the other judges of the Court' (i.e., sitting judges of the Supreme Court), not from retired judges. Retired judges sitting ad-hoc are covered under Article 128.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers and functions of an Acting Chief Justice of India:
1. An Acting Chief Justice exercises all the powers, duties, and administrative privileges of the Chief Justice of India.
2. An Acting Chief Justice is barred from hearing matters related to fundamental rights enforcement under Article 32.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: An Acting CJI steps fully into the office and performs all duties and wields all administrative and judicial powers of the CJI. Statement 2 is incorrect: There are no jurisdictional limitations or bars placed on an Acting CJI; they can hear any matter that a regular CJI can hear, including writ petitions under Article 32.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India explicitly prescribes a fixed tenure of six months for an Acting Chief Justice of India.
2. The salary payable to the Acting Chief Justice of India is equivalent to that of the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution does not prescribe any fixed or maximum tenure for an Acting CJI; it lasts until the regular CJI resumes duties or a new CJI is appointed. Statement 2 is correct: Under the Second Schedule and related statutes, while acting as CJI, the judge receives the salary and allowances corresponding to the office of the Chief Justice of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional provisions and judicial administration:
1. Article 126 is invoked only when the office of the Chief Justice of India is vacant, and cannot be used if the CJI is merely on temporary leave.
2. The appointment under Article 126 is made by the President of India under their hand and seal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 126 explicitly states that an Acting CJI can be appointed not only when the office is vacant, but also when the CJI is 'by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of his office'. Thus, temporary leave or illness also triggers Article 126. Statement 2 is correct: As with all constitutional appointments by the President, the warrant of appointment for an Acting CJI is issued under the hand and seal of the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A judge appointed as Acting Chief Justice of India must take a fresh oath specifically mentioning the office of Acting Chief Justice before assuming charge.
2. The convention of appointing the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court as Acting Chief Justice has statutory backing under the Judges (Inquiry) Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is incorrect because Supreme Court judges already take a constitutional oath under the Third Schedule upon initial appointment, and no fresh or separate oath is prescribed or required for acting temporarily as CJI. Statement 2 is incorrect because the seniority convention for Acting CJI (and regular CJI) stems from established judicial convention and constitutional practice, not from the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 (which deals with the removal of judges).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional safeguards surrounding the Supreme Court leadership:
1. Article 126 ensures that judicial administration does not come to a standstill during the temporary absence or vacancy of the Chief Justice.
2. The President has absolute discretionary power under Article 126 to appoint any Supreme Court judge, bypassing seniority without any constitutional convention constraining them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The primary purpose of Article 126 is to prevent administrative paralysis and ensure the continuous, uninterrupted functioning of the Supreme Court. Statement 2 is incorrect: While the text of Article 126 says 'such one of the other judges of the Court as the President deems fit', constitutional convention, reinforced by the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (1993) case and subsequent rulings regarding judicial appointments and independence, strongly binds the executive to follow the principle of seniority in appointing the Acting CJI, preventing arbitrary executive interference.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing Acting CJI (Article 126) and Ad-hoc Judges (Article 127):
1. Both offices are meant to deal with temporary exigencies in the Supreme Court.
2. While an Acting CJI performs the duties of the head of the institution, an ad-hoc judge is appointed solely to constitute a quorum for Supreme Court sittings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Statement 1 highlights that both provisions are designed to handle temporary shortages or vacancies in judicial manpower. Statement 2 accurately distinguishes their core mandates: Article 126 provides leadership replacement for the CJI, whereas Article 127 addresses quorum deficiencies by summoning High Court judges qualified to sit as Supreme Court judges.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative role of an Acting Chief Justice:
1. An Acting Chief Justice has the authority to make references to the President under Article 143 (Advisory Jurisdiction).
2. An Acting Chief Justice cannot recommend names for the appointment of new Supreme Court judges through the Collegium during their temporary tenure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: As they perform all the duties of the Chief Justice, an Acting CJI can preside over benches dealing with presidential references under Article 143 or handle institutional communications. Statement 2 is incorrect: An Acting CJI heads the Supreme Court Collegium and fully participates in recommending appointments and transfers of judges, as judicial vacancies and administration cannot be frozen simply because the permanent CJI is temporarily absent or a transition is underway.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The provisions of Article 126 apply mutatis mutandis to High Courts under Article 223 for the appointment of Acting Chief Justices of High Courts.
2. Both Article 126 and Article 223 empower the President of India to make these temporary judicial appointments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 223 specifically deals with the appointment of an Acting Chief Justice for a High Court, mirroring Article 126 conceptually, but it is a distinct article in Part VI of the Constitution, not a mutatis mutandis application of Article 126. Statement 2 is correct: Both Article 126 (for Supreme Court) and Article 223 (for High Courts) vest the power of appointing Acting Chief Justices in the President of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the cessation of office of an Acting Chief Justice of India:
1. The tenure of an Acting Chief Justice automatically terminates as soon as a permanent Chief Justice assumes office or the incumbent CJI returns from leave.
2. An Acting Chief Justice can be removed from office before the expiry of their temporary assignment through a formal parliamentary impeachment motion similar to that of a Supreme Court judge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The office of Acting CJI is inherently temporary and ends immediately when the regular CJI returns or a new CJI is appointed. Statement 2 is incorrect: An Acting CJI does not require a separate impeachment process to cease functioning as Acting CJI; their temporary assignment ends by operation of law/constitution when the regular CJI resumes office. Furthermore, removal of a Supreme Court judge (which an Acting CJI remains substantively) requires a presidential order following an address by both Houses of Parliament supported by special majority under Article 124(4), not a separate mechanism for the 'acting' assignment.
